description: We are a multidisciplinary team conformed by young students from San Juan, Argentina, focused on social integration, education and a fierce love for the stars.
summary:
Astrolife is a strategy and resource management based videogame where the player takes the role of an astronaut inspired by Alyssa Carson. We aim to catch the attention of children of the ages between 9 and 12 so they learn about the decision-making behind each mission.
We tackle the challenge of creating a videogame that presents interactive situations that go from base repairs to climatic phenomena, forcing kids to come up with strategies to survive and learn that each consequence will affect the objective of survival.
It is important because utilizing fun resources strenghtens the learning curve and fun tasks augments the engagement and desire of knowledge of the kids, kids who learn educating space content verified and published by NASA, it tackles resource management which creates awareness on the importance of a real mission and it explores real time decision making that will determine the mission’s success.
We hope that this project can reach provincial educational centers such as the Anchipurac Enviromental Center or to the El Leoncito Astronomical Complex (CASLEO).
details:
“Astrolife” works as an interactive experience straight from your web browser about survival in mars, the game can be categorized as a roguelike, strategy, point and click, 2D resource manager. Where each adventure is completely different from the previous one, incentivizing replayability. In this game there will be events that will let the player make decisions regarding their own survival and maintenance of their base as each Martian sun goes by, promoting the mindset that all your actions have consequences. ¿Want to water your green house? You’ll have to spend water. ¿Did a sandstorm happen? Your base now has less power. Different climate events such as; marsquake’s, sandstorms and sunstorms that’ll affect the game's trajectory.

The main character is inspired by Alyssa Carson, an aspiring NASA astronaut whose objective is to participate in a possible martian mission in the decade of the 2030’s (Design Museum, Circa 2019). We believe that if the first person to take a step on mars is a woman, it will inspire and incentivize many young girls to aspire to become astronauts themselves by being represented in the space company that many dream of. The game has a lot of accessibility potential in terms of scale, we plan future ideas such as a new level that takes place on the moon and accessibility for people with different disabilities, many of these being the addition of logos or visual alerts for people that are hard of hearing or people who are colorblind, as well as auditory resources for people with sight problems and break language barriers by translating the game to different languages, we believe that every child should be able to enjoy and dream of being an astronaut.

We also count with the help of Opportunity, the rover that NASA left stranded in mars due to the lack of energy in consequence of the sandstorms that stained its solar panels (NASA, s. f.), we thought it would be great to rescue this successful rover and return it to its glory days, the game takes place near Perseverance Valley, where said rover rests (NASA, 2019).

As a team we believe that the creativity that drives our project is highly interdisciplinary and complete, our software and tool focus was primarily html, css and javascript for the game’s code coupled with artificial intelligence to smooth technical details without the need to complicate the project because we believe it is more important to communicate that an idea works before its technical side and AI has helped us a lot in this step, we utilized ChatGPT asistance to code the videogame and we hand drawed all the images used in the 30 seconds presentation video with Clip Studio Paint Pro (free available drawing software). Said presentation was made using the free video-making editing software Capcut, the game’s assets were entirely hand drawn by our art team with the use of graphic tablets and the art software Clip Studio Paint Pro, the interfaces and fonts were done with code to not overburden our team with more work, again, the main idea was to keep it simple but filled with true cited information (Redacted in an accessible way for younger audiences). If it weren't for it we wouldn’t have the logbook or the necessary information if we didn’t make use of the literary resources offered by NASA and the collaborators of the NASA Space App Challenge.

We believe this project is creative because of the variety of roles needed for its production. It develops children’s ability of quick decision-making due to the different consequences that demand strategizing, the resources being limited allow measurement of the cost that using them or dividing them for the sake of the integrity of the base would bring.

The information is presented in a way that is easy to comprehend but also to not lose precision, which enhances and reinforces academic learning without the need to use an essay or boring texts. For this, in the videogame we incorporated a “logbook” where important info is stored, for example, if our zinnia plant found in the base, the only plant to have completed a cycle in the space inside the ISS (Nasa, 2016), wither dues to humidity as it happened before, in the logbook you’ll see a new entry that talks about how humidity can affect plant in microgravity (NASA & Hobson, 2016, #).

The impact we want to generate is not only to catch the attention of children, but to also inspire them to learn more about the mission, the preparations behind them, each planet and the universe itself and so they have a strong fun source of information where they can find facts verified by NASA. We hope that by implementing a main character based on a woman we can also motivate young girls to orient themselves towards science, bringing them a role model during their academic years and to also find themselves represented in the world of videogames.

To promote the belief that you can make your dreams come true, above all if there are children who wish to work in NASA as a scientist and for those that live with physical characteristics that think it defines them or prevents them from reaching their goals. Reaching a level of inclusion inside the game and later reflected in the school life and professional life.

As a team we had many factors to keep in mind during the production of the project, we had to base all of our collected knowledge from sources given by NASA or associated organizations and to find a way to represent this information in a way that it is comprehensible and not lose the users attention, to solve this we combined text with sounds and colors but we didn’t only focus on text but we also added other sensory effects, achieving a friendly interface for children. Another factor was accessibility. To solve this, we made the videogame playable through a browser, so both kids and adults could easily access it. It can also be played without the need of creating an account. Another factor to keep in mind was the scale, our idea didn’t stop at Mars only, for we plan to explore space itself, adding more functions and additional addons so that the game adapts to every child, for colour blindness we would implement color correction filters that let the user adjust the color palette according to their visual deficiency, adjust the speed of the actions so it adapts to the user and for people with hearing disabilities we’d add vibrations to accompany the sounds.
